G1000.def:
βολή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(βάλλω), [in LXX: Genèse 21:16 (טחה), 2Ma.5:3, 3Ma.5:26 * ;] 
a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw: Luc 22:41.†

G1001.def:
βολίζω 
(βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead), 
to heave the lead, take soundings: Actes 27:28.†

G1002.def:
βολίς, -ίδος, ἡ 
(βάλλω), [in LXX for חֵץ, יָרָה, etc. ;] 
a dart, javelin: Hébreux 12:20, Rec. (LXX).†

G1003.def:
Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז), 
Boaz (Ruth 2:1): Matthieu 1:5, Luc 3:32.†

G1004.def:
βόρβορος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Je 45(38):6 (טִיט)* ;] 
mud, filth: 2 Pierre 2:22.†

G1005.def:
βορρᾶς, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified), 
[in LXX for צָפוֹן ;] 
__1. Boreas, the North wind. 
__2. the north: Luc 13:29, Apocalypse 21:13.
†

G1006.def:
βόσκω, 
[in LXX for רעה ;] 
prop., of a herdsman, to feed: Matthieu 8:33, Marc 5:14, Luc 8:34 15:15; metaphorically, of Christian pastoral care, Jean 21:15, 17. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze: Matthieu 8:30, Marc 5:11, Luc 8:32.†
SYN.: ποιμαίνειν, to tend, shepherd, a wider term, including oversight as well as feeding (see Tr., Syn., §xxv).

G1007.def:
Βοσόρ see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר), 
Beor, father of Balaam: 2 Pierre 2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).†

G1008.def:
βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ 
(βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב, דֶשֶׁא, חָצִיר ;] 
__1. grass, fodder. 
__2. green herb: Hébreux 6:7.†
SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable.

G1009.def:
βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX for אֶשְׁכֹּל ;] 
a cluster of grapes: Apocalypse 14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .†

G1010.def:
βουλευτής, -οῦ, ὁ 
(βουλεύω), [in LXX: Job 3:14 12:17 (יעץ)* ;] 
a councillor, a senator; of a member of the Sanhedrin: Marc 15:34, Luc 23:50.†

G1011.def:
βουλεύω 
(βουλή), [in LXX chiefly for יעץ ;] 
to take counsel, deliberate, resolve. In mid., 
__1. to take counsel with oneself, consider: before εἰ, Luc 14:31. 
__2. to determine with oneself, resolve: with inf., Actes 5:33 27:39; with accusative, 2 Corinthiens 1:17; before ἵνα, Jean 11:53 12:10 (cf. παρα-, συμ-).
†

G1012.def:
βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(βούλομαι), [in LXX frequently for עֵצָה ;] 
counsel, purpose (in cl., esp. of the gods): Luc 23:51, Actes 4:28 5:38 19:1 27:12, 42; pl., 1 Corinthiens 4:5; of the Divine purpose, Hébreux 6:17; τ. βουλὴν τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Éphésiens 1:11; β. τ. Θεοῦ, Luc 7:30, Actes 2:23 13:36 20:27.†

G1013.def:
βούλημα, -τος, τό 
(βούλομαι), [in LXX: Proverbes 9:10 (דַּעַת), 2Ma.15:5, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] 
purpose, will: Actes 27:43, Romains 9:19, 1 Pierre 4:3.†
SYN.: θέλημα.

G1014.def:
βούλομαι, 
[in LXX for חפץ, אבה, יעץ, etc. ;] 
to will, wish, desire, purpose, be minded, implying more strongly than θέλω (which see), the deliberate exercise of volition (see Hort on Jacques 1:18): with inf. (M, Pr., 205; Bl., §69, 4), Marc 15:15, Actes 5:28, 33 12:4 15:37 17:20 18:15, 27 19:30 22:30 23:28 27:43 28:18, 2 Corinthiens 1:15, 1 Timothée 6:9, Hébreux 6:17, II Jhn.12, 3Jo.10, Ju 5; with accusative, 2 Corinthiens 1:17; with accusative and inf., Philippiens 1:12, 1 Timothée 2:8 5:14, Tite 3:8, 2 Pierre 3:9; of the will making choice between alternatives, Matthieu 1:19 11:27, Luc 10:22, Actes 25:20, 1 Corinthiens 12:11, Jacques 3:4 4:4; εἰ βούλει (cl., a courteous phrase = θέλεις, colloq.; Bl., §21, 8; LS, see word), Luc 22:42; with subjc., adding force to a question of deliberation (Bl., §64, 6), Jean 18:39; βουληθείς, of set purpose (see Hort, in l.), Jacques 1:18; impf., ἐβουλόμην (= cl. βουλοίμην ἄν; Bl., §63, 5; Lft., Phm. 13), Actes 25:22, Phm 13 (see also Cremer, 143).†

G1015.def:
βουνός, -οῦ, ὁ (a Cyrenaїc word, Hdt., iv, 199), 
[in LXX chiefly for גִּבְעָה ;] 
a hill: Luc 3:5 (LXX) 23:30.†

G1016.def:
βοῦς, βοός, ὁ, ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקָר ;] 
an ox, a cow: Luc 13:15 14:5, 19 Jean 2:14, 15 1 Corinthiens 9:9" (LXX), 1 Timothée 5:18.†

G1017.def:
βραβεῖον, -ου, τό 
(βραβεύς, an umpire), 
a prize in the games: 1 Corinthiens 9:24; metaphorically, of the Christian's reward, Philippiens 3:14.†

G1018.def:
βραβεύω 
(βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;] 
__(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence, 
__(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Colossiens 3:15; 
__(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω).
†

G1019.def:
βραδύνω 
(βραδύς), [in LXX: Genèse 43:10 (מההּ hith.), Deutéronome 7:10, Ésaïe 46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;] 
__1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with). 
__2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1 Timothée 3:15, 2 Pierre 3:9.
†

G1020.def:
βραδυπλοέω, -ῶ 
(βραδύς, πλοῦς), 
to sail slowly: Actes 27:7.†

G1021.def:
βραδύς, -εῖα, -ύ, 
slow: εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, Jacques 1:19; metaphorically, of the understanding: β. τ. καρδίᾳ, assoc. with ἀνόητος, Luc 24:25.†

G1022.def:
1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G1023.def:
βραχίων, -ὀνος, ὁ, 
[in LXX, β. Κυρίου, frequently for זְרוֹעַ יהוָֹה ;] 
the arm; as in OT, β. Κυρίου, metaphorically, for the Divine power: Luc 1:51, Jean 12:38" (LXX), Actes 13:17.†

G1025.def:
βρέφος, -ους, τό, 
[in LXX: Sir.19:11, 1Ma.1:61, 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.5:49, 4Ma.4:25 * ;] 
__1. an unborn child: Luc 1:41, 44. 
__2. a newborn child, a babe: Luc 2:12, 16 18:15, Actes 7:19, 1 Pierre 2:2; ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy, 2 Timothée 3:15.
†

G1026.def:
βρέχω, 
[in LXX chiefly for מטר ;] 
__1. to wet: Luc 7:38, 44. 
__2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): Matthieu 5:45; trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, Luc 17:29; impers., βρέχει, it rains: Jacques 5:17; with ὐετός as subj., Apocalypse 11:6.
†

G1027.def:
βροντή, -ῆς, ἡ, 
[in LXX for רַעַם ;] 
thunder: Marc 3:17, Jean 12:29, Apocalypse 4:5 6:1 8:5 10:3, 4 11:19 14:2 16:18 19:6.†

G1028.def:
βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(βρέχω), [in LXX: Psa.67 (68):9, 104 (105):32 (גֶּשֶׁם)* ;] 
__1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77). 
__2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Matthieu 7:25, 27.
†

G1029.def:
βρόχος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 6:5 (יָד) 7:21 (חֵלֶק) 22:25 (מוֹקֵשׁ), 3Ma.4:8 * ;] 
a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaphorically, a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): 1 Corinthiens 7:35.†

G1030.def:
βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(βρύχω), [in LXX: Proverbes 19:12 (נַהַם), Sir.51:3 * ;] 
a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Matthieu 8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luc 13:28.†

G1031.def:
βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω), 
[in LXX: Job 16:10(9), Psa.34 (35):16 36 (37):12 111 (112):10, La 2:16 (חרק)* ;] 
__1. to bite or eat greedily. 
__2. to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Actes 7:54.
†

G1032.def:
βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac., 
to be full to bursting; 
__1. of the earth producing vegetation. 
__2. Of plants putting forth buds. 
__3. Of springs, to gush with water: Jacques 3:11.
†

G1033.def:
βρῶμα, -τος, τό (cf. βιβρώσκω), 
[in LXX chiefly for אֹכֶל ;] 
food: Romains 14:15, 20 1 Corinthiens 8:8, 13 10:3; pl., Matthieu 14:15, Marc 7:19, Luc 3:11 9:13, 1 Corinthiens 6:13, 1 Timothée 4:3, Hébreux 9:10 13:9; trop., of spiritual food, Jean 4:34, 1 Corinthiens 3:2 (cf. βρῶσις).†

G1034.def:
βρώσιμος, -ον 
(βρῶσις), [in LXX: Lévitique 19:23, Néhémie 9:25, Eze.47:12 (מַאֲכָל)* ;] 
eatable: Luc 24:41.†

G1035.def:
βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω), 
[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל ;] 
__1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Romains 14:17, Colossiens 2:16 (see Lft., ICC, in l.); with genitive obj., 1 Corinthiens 8:4; metaphorically, corrosion, rust: Matthieu 6:19, 20. 
__2. As also in cl. (Hom., al.) = βρῶμα, food: Jean 6:27a, 2 Corinthiens 9:10, Colossiens 2:16 (EV, but see supr.). Hébreux 12:16; metaphorically, of spiritual nourishment, Jean 4:32 6:27b, 55.†

G1036.def:
βυθίζω 
(βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;] 
trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1 Timothée 6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luc 5:7.†

G1037.def:
βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Exode 15:5, Néhémie 9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Psa.67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;] 
__1. the bottom. 
__2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2 Corinthiens 11:25.
†

G1038.def:
βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης, 
a tanner: Actes 9:43 10:6, 32.†

G1039.def:
βύσσινος, -η, -ον 
(βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;] 
made of βύσσος, fine linen: Apocalypse 18:12, 16 19:8, 14.†

G1040.def:
βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ), 
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ ;] 
byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Luc 16:19.†

G1041.def:
βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה ;] 
__1. any raised place, a platform. 
__2. an altar: Actes 17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and see DB, i, 75).
†

G1042.def:
Γαββαθα (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl., 
Gabbatha, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (DB, see word; Dalman, Words, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, stone pavement: Jean 19:13.†

G1043.def:
Γαβριήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, hero of God), 
the archangel Gabriel: Luc 1:19, 26.†

G1044.def:
γάγγραινα, -ης, ἡ, 
a gangrene, an eating sore, which leads to mortification: 2 Timothée 2:17.†

G1045.def:
Γάδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גָּד), 
Gad (Genèse 30:11 49:13, al.): Apocalypse 7:5.†

G1046.def:
Γαδαρηνός, -ή, -όν 
(Γαδαρά, Gadara, the capital of Peræa), 
Gadarene, of Gadara: Matthieu 8:28 (Rec. Γεργεσηνῶν), Marc 5:1, Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν), Luc 8:26, 37 Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν).†

G1047.def:
γάζα, -ης, ἡ (a Persian word), 
[in LXX for גִּנְזִין, II Esther 5:17 6:1 7:20, 21, Esther 4:7; גִּזְבָּר, II Esther 7:21; Ésaïe 39:2 * ;] 
treasure: Actes 8:27.†

G1048.def:
Γάζα -ης, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה), 
Gaza, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines: Actes 8:26.†

G1049.def:
γαζο-φυλάκιον, -ου, τό 
(γάζα, φυλακή), [in LXX chiefly for לִשְׁכָּה, נִשְׁכָּה (4Ki.23:11, al.), once for גְּנָזִים (Esther 3:9); το͂ γ., τᾶ γ., of a temple treasury, Néhémie 10:37, 2Ma.3:6, al. ;] 
treasury: also, apparently, the trumpet-shaped chests into which the peoples' temple-offerings were thrown (DB, iv, 96; DCG, ii, 748): Marc 12:41, 43 Luc 21:1, Jean 8:20.†

G1050G.def:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), 
Gaius, the name of a Christian; 
__1. of Macedonia: Actes 19:29. 
__2. Of Derbe: Actes 20:4. 
__3. Of Corinth: Romains 16:23, 1 Corinthiens 1:14. 
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
†

G1050H.def:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), 
Gaius, the name of a Christian; 
__1. of Macedonia: Actes 19:29. 
__2. Of Derbe: Actes 20:4. 
__3. Of Corinth: Romains 16:23, 1 Corinthiens 1:14. 
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
†

G1050I.def:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), 
Gaius, the name of a Christian; 
__1. of Macedonia: Actes 19:29. 
__2. Of Derbe: Actes 20:4. 
__3. Of Corinth: Romains 16:23, 1 Corinthiens 1:14. 
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
†

G1050J.def:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.), 
Gaius, the name of a Christian; 
__1. of Macedonia: Actes 19:29. 
__2. Of Derbe: Actes 20:4. 
__3. Of Corinth: Romains 16:23, 1 Corinthiens 1:14. 
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
†

G1051.def:
γάλα, -ακτος, τό 
[in LXX for חלב ;] 
milk: 1 Corinthiens 9:7. Metaphorical, of elementary Christian teaching: 1 Corinthiens 3:2, Hébreux 5:12, 13; τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γ., the rational (spiritual) genuine milk (see Hort, in l.), 1 Pierre 2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, see ICC, in l.).†

G1052.def:
Γαλάτης, -ου, ὁ (originally syn. with cl. Κέλτης; cf. 1Ma.8:2, and see next word), 
a Galatian: Galates 3:1.†

G1053.def:
Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ, 
Galatia; 
__1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C). 
__2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): 1 Corinthiens 16:1, Galates 1:2, 2 Timothée 4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1 Pierre 1:1.
†

G1054.def:
Γαλατικός, -ή, -όν (see previous word), 
Galatian, belonging to Galatia: Actes 16:6 18:23.†

G1055.def:
γαλήνη, -ης, ἡ, 
a calm: Matthieu 8:26, Marc 4:39, Luc 8:24.†

G1056G.def:
Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), 
Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Matthieu 4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Matthieu 15:29 (cf. Jean 6:1).

G1056H.def:
Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district), 
Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Matthieu 4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Matthieu 15:29 (cf. Jean 6:1).

G1057.def:
Γαλιλαῖος, -αία, -αῖον, 
Galilæan: Matthieu 26:69, Marc 14:70, Luc 13:1, 2 22:59, 23:6, Jean 4:45, Actes 1:11 2:7 5:37.†

G1058.def:
Γαλλίων, -ωνος, ὁ, 
Gallio, proconsul of Achaia: Actes 18:12, 14 17.†

G1059.def:
Γαμαλιήλ, ὁ (Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל), 
Gamaliel the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law: Actes 5:34 22:3.†

G1060.def:
γαμέω, -ῶ, 
[in LXX: Esther 10:3, 2Ma.14:25, 4Ma.16:9 * ;] 
to marry; 
__1. of the man, to marry, take to wife (ducere): absol., Matthieu 19:10 22:25, 30 24:38, Marc 12:25, Luc 17:27, 20:34, 35, 1 Corinthiens 7:28, 33; with accusative: Matthieu 5:32 19:9, Marc 6:17 10:11, Luc 14:20 16:18. 
__2. Of the woman, 
__(a) mid. (and in late writers, pass.), to give oneself in marriage, marry (nubere): 1 Corinthiens 7:39; 
__(b) in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 159), act. (as of the man), to marry: absol., 1 Corinthiens 7:28, 34 1 Timothée 5:11, 14. with accusative, Marc 10:12. 
__3. Of both sexes: absol., 1 Timothée 4:3, 1 Corinthiens 7:9, 10 36.
†

G1061.def:
γαμίζω 
(γάμος), 
to give in marriage, a daughter: 1 Corinthiens 7:38. Pass., Matthieu 22:30 24:38, Marc 12:25, Luc 17:27 20:35 (WH, mg., γαμίσκονται; cf. γαμίζω).†

G1062.def:
γάμος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX for מִשְׁתֶּה ;] 
__1. a wedding, esp. a wedding-feast: Matthieu 22:8, 10 11, 12, Jean 2:1-3, Apocalypse 19:7, 9; pl. (Field, Notes, 16), Matthieu 22:2-4, 9 25:10, Luc 12:36 14:8. 
__2. marriage: Hébreux 13:4 (Cremer, 666).
†

G1063.def:
γάρ, 
co-ordinating particle, contr. of γε ἄρα, 
verily then, hence, in truth, indeed, yea, then, why, and when giving a reason or explanation, for, the usage in NT being in general accord with that of cl.; 
__1. explicative and epexegetic: Matthieu 4:18 19:12, Marc 1:16 5:42 16:4, Luc 11:3o, Romains 7:1, 1 Corinthiens 16:5, al. 
__2. Conclusive, in questions, answers and exclamations: Matthieu 9:5 27:23, Luc 9:25 22:27, Jean 9:30, Actes 8:31 16:37 19:35, Romains 15:26, 1 Corinthiens 9:10, Philippiens 1:18 (Ellic., in l.), 1 Thessaloniciens 2:20, al. 
__3. Causal: Matthieu 1:21 2:2, 5, 6, 3:23, Marc 1:22, 9:6, Luc 1:15, 18, Jean 2:25, Actes 2:25, Romains 1:9, 11, 1 Corinthiens 11:5, Apocalypse 1:3, al.; giving the reason for a command or prohibition, Matthieu 2:20 3:9, Romains 13:11, Colossiens 3:3, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:3, al.; where the cause is contained in an interrog. statement, Luc 22:27, Romains 3:3 4:3, 1 Corinthiens 10:29; καὶ γάρ, for also, Marc 10:45, Luc 6:32, 1 Corinthiens 5:7, al. id. as in cl. = etenim, where the καί loses its connective force (Bl., §78, 6; Kühner 3, ii, 854f.), Marc 14:70, Luc 1:66 22:37, 2 Corinthiens 13:4. The proper place of γάρ is after the first word in a clause, but in poets it often comes third or fourth, and so in late prose: 2 Corinthiens 1:19. Yet "not the number but the nature of the word after which it stands is the point to be noticed" (see Thayer, see word).

G1064.def:
γαστήρͅ, -τρός, ἡ, 
[in LXX for בֶּטֶן, ἐν γ. ἔχειν for הרה, ἐν γ. λαμβάνειν for חרה ;] 
__1. the belly: metaphorically, a glutton, Tite 1:12. 
__2. the womb: ἐν γ. ἔχειν, to be with child, Matthieu 1:18, 23" (LXX) 24:19, Marc 13:17, Luc 21:23, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:3, Apocalypse 12:2; εν γ. συλλαμβ., to conceive, Luc 1:31.
†

G1065.def:
γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important (Thayer, see word), 
indeed, at least, even (but not always translatable into English); 
__1. used alone: Luc 11:8 18:5 Romains 8:32. 
__2. More frequently with other particles: αλλά γε, Luc 24:21, 1 Corinthiens 9:2; ἄρα γε, Matthieu 7:20 17:26, Actes 17:27; ἆρά γε, Actes 8:30; εἴ γε (Rec. εἴγε), 2 Corinthiens 5:3, Galates 3:4, Éphésiens 3:2 4:21, Colossiens 1:23 (see Meyer, Ellic., on Ga, Eph, ll. with; Lft., on Ga, Col, ll. with); εἰ δὲ μήγε, following an affirmation, Matthieu 6:1, Luc 10:6 13:9; a negation, Matthieu 9:17, Luc 5:36, 37 14:32, 2 Corinthiens 11:16; καί γε (Rec. καίγε, cl. καὶ . . . γε), Luc 19:42 (WH om.), Actes 2:18 17:27; καίτοιγε (L καίτοι γε, Tr. καί τοι γε), Jean 4:2; μενοῦνγε (see see word); μήτι γε, see: μήτι; ὄφελόν, 1 Corinthiens 4:8.
†

G1066.def:
Γεδεών, ὁ, indecl. in LXX and NT, in FlJ, Ant., see 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן), 
Gideon (Jdg.6-8): Hébreux 11:32.†

G1068.def:
Γεθσημασεί (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, oil-press), 
Gethsemane: called in Jean 18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Matthieu 26:36, Marc 14:32.†

G1069.def:
γείτων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ 
(γῆ), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן ;] 
a neighbour: Luc 14:12 15:6, 9 Jean 9:8.†

G1070.def:
γελάω, -ῶ, 
[in LXX chiefly for צחק, שׂחק ;] 
to laugh: Luc 6:25; fut., γελάσω) (M, Pr., 154), ib. 21 (cf. κατα-γελάω).†

G1071.def:
γέλως, -ωτος, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for שְׂחוֹק ;] 
laughter: Jacques 4:9.†

G1072.def:
γεμίζω 
(γέμω), [in LXX: Genèse 45:17 (טען), 3Ma.5:47, 4Ma.3:14 * ;] 
to fill; 
__1. properly, of a ship (Thuc, al.): Marc 4:37 (pass.). 
__2. In late writers, generally (MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), with accusative, before genitive, Marc 15:36, Jean 2:7 6:13, Apocalypse 15:8; ἀπό, Luc 15:16, Rec. WH, mg.; ἐκ, Luc 15:16, WH, Apocalypse 8:5. Pass., absol.: Luc 14:23.
†

G1073.def:
γέμω (used only in present and impf.), 
[in LXX for מלא, נשׂא ;] 
to be full; 
__1. properly, of a ship (Xen.). 
__2. Generally (Plat., al.), 
__(a) with genitive of thing(s): Matthieu 23:27, Luc 11:39, Romains 3:14" (LXX), Apocalypse 4:6, 8 5:8 15:7 17:3 (Rec.) 4 21:9 
__(b) before ἐκ: Matthieu 23:25; 
__(with) with accusative of thing(s) (called a solecism in WM, 251; Bl., §36, 4), as in later Gk. from Byz. to Mod. times (Jannaris, Gr., 1319): Apocalypse 17:3.
†

G1075.def:
γενεαλογέω, -ῶ 
(γενεά, λέγω), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 5:1 (יחשׁ)* ;] 
to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., before ἐκ: Hébreux 7:6.†

G1076.def:
γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (see previous word); 
__1. the making of a pedigree. 
__2. a genealogy: pl., 1 Timothée 1:4, Tite 3:9 (see CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141).
†

G1077.def:
γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (γένεσις); 
__1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead. 
__2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., see MM, Exp., x; cf. also Ῥutherford, NPhr., 184): Matthieu 14:6, Marc 6:21.
†

G1078.def:
γένεσις, -εως, ἡ 
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלֵדֹת ;] 
__1. origin, lineage: βίβλος γενέσεως (as in Genèse 2:4a 5:1), Matthieu 1:1. 
__2. birth: Matthieu 1:18, Luc 1:14 (Rec. γέννησις); πρόσωπον τῆς γ., face of his birth ("what God made him to be," Hort., in l.), Jacques 1:23; ὁ τροχὸς τῆς γ., the wheel (course) of birth or creation ("the wheel of man's nature according to its original Divine purpose," Hort), Jacques 3:6.
†

G1079.def:
γενετή, -ῆς, ἡ = γενεή, Ion. for γενεά, 
[in LXX: Lévitique 25:47 (עֵקֶר מִשְׁפָּחָו), Esther 4:17 * ;] 
birth: ἐκ γ., Jean 9:1.†

G1080.def:
γεννάω, -ῶ 
(γέννα, poët. for γένος), [in LXX chiefly for ילד ;] 
__1. of the father, to beget: with accusative, Matthieu 1:1-16, Actes 7:8, 29; before ἐκ, Matthieu 1:3, 5, 6. 
__2. Of the mother, to bring forth, bear: Luc 1:13, 57 23:29, Jean 16:21; εἰς δουλείαν, Galates 4:24. Pass. 
__(1) to be begotten: Matthieu 1:20; 
__(2) to be born: Matthieu 2:1, 4 19:12 26:24, Marc 14:21, Luc 1:35, Jean 3:4, Actes 7:20, Romains 9:11, Hébreux 11:23; before εἰς, Jean 16:21 18:37, 2 Pierre 2:12; ἐν, Actes 2:8 22:3, (ἁμαρτίαις), Jean 9:34; ἀπό, Hébreux 11:12 (WH, mg., ἐγεν-); ἐκ, Jean 1:13 3:6 8:41; with adj., τυφλὸς γ., Jean 9:2; [Ῥωμαῖος ], Actes 22:28; κατὰ σάρκα: κ. πνεῦμα: Galates 4:29. Metaphorical; μάχας, 2 Timothée 2:23; ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα, 1 Corinthiens 4:15, (ὅν), Phm 10; in quotation, Psaumes 2:7 (LXX), Actes 13:33, Hébreux 1:5 5:5; of Christians as begotten of God, born again: Jean 1:13 3:3, 5-8, 1 Jean 2:29 3:9 4:7 5:1, 4, 18 (cf. ἀνα-γεννάω); (Cremer, 146).

G1081G.def:
γέννημα, -τος, τό 
(γεννάω), [in LXX chiefly for תְּבוּאָה ;] 
offspring of men or animals: ἐχιδνῶν, Matthieu 3:7 12:34 23:33, Luc 3:7 (and elsewhere in Rec. for γένημα, which see).†

G1082.def:
Γεννησαρέτ (Rec. Γενησ-, Mk, l.with; Targ. גְּנֵיסַר), 
[in LXX: Γεννησάρ (as in some MSS. Mt, Mk), 1Ma.11:67 * ;] 
Gennesaret, a fertile plain on W. shore of the Sea of Galilee; ἡ γῆ, Matthieu 14:34, Marc 6:53; ἡ λίμνη (יָם כִּנֶּרֶת, Nombres 34:11, elsewhere ἡ θάλασσα τ. Γαλιλαίας, Marc 1:16; ἡ θ. τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jean 6:1), Luc 5:1.†

G1084.def:
γεννητός, -ή -όν 
(γεννάω), [in LXX: Job 11:2, 12 14:1 15:14 25:4 (ילד)* ;] 
begotten, born: pl., γ. γυναικῶν (cf. יְלוּד אִשָּׁה, Job 14:1), periphrasis for mankind, Matthieu 11:11, Luc 7:28 (Cremer, 147).

G1085G.def:
γένος, -ους, τό 
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc. ;] 
__1. family: Actes 4:6 7:13 13:26. 
__2. offspring: Actes 17:28, 29 Apocalypse 22:16. 
__3. race, nation; Marc 7:28, Actes 4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, 2 Corinthiens 11:26, Philippiens 3:5, Galates 1:14, 1 Pierre 2:9. 
__4. kind, sort, class: Matthieu 13:47 17:21, Rec., Marc 9:29, 1 Corinthiens 12:10, 28 14:10.
†

G1085H.def:
γένος, -ους, τό 
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc. ;] 
__1. family: Actes 4:6 7:13 13:26. 
__2. offspring: Actes 17:28, 29 Apocalypse 22:16. 
__3. race, nation; Marc 7:28, Actes 4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, 2 Corinthiens 11:26, Philippiens 3:5, Galates 1:14, 1 Pierre 2:9. 
__4. kind, sort, class: Matthieu 13:47 17:21, Rec., Marc 9:29, 1 Corinthiens 12:10, 28 14:10.
†

G1086G.def:
Γεργασηνός, -ή, -όν, 
Gerasene, of Gerasa, not the G. of Decapolis, 30 m. S.E. of the Lake, but a Gerasa or Gergesa (perh. the mod. Kersa) on E. shore; as subst., pl. οἱ Γ., Marc 5:1, Luc 8:26, 37 (Γεργεσηνῶν, RV, mg. 1; Γαδαρηνῶν, RV, mg. 2).†

G1087.def:
γερουσία, -ας, ἡ 
(γέρων), [in LXX (Hex. only in OT) for זָקֵן ;] 
a council of elders, senate; in NT, of the Sanhedrin (Cl. Rev., i, 43f.; DB, ext., 99): Actes 5:21.†

G1088.def:
γέρων, -οντος, ὁ, 
[in LXX for זָקֵן ;] 
an old man: Jean 3:4.†

G1089.def:
γεύω, γεύομαι, 
[in LXX chiefly for טעם ;] 
to make to taste. Mid., to taste eat: absol., Actes 10:10 20:11, Colossiens 2:21; with genitive, Matthieu 27:34, Luc 14:24, Actes 23:14; with accusative (not cl., but see Westc, Heb., l.with; M, Pr., 66, 245), Jean 2:9. Metaphorical, Hébreux 6:4; ῥῆμα θεοῦ, Hébreux 6:5 (on case, see supr., and cf. Milligan, NTD, 68) θανάτου (cf. Talmudic טַעַם מִיתָה), Matthieu 16:28, Marc 9:1, Luc 9:27, Jean 8:52, Hébreux 2:9; before ὅτι, 1 Pierre 2:3 (Cremer, 148).†

G1090.def:
γεωργέω, -ῶ 
(γεωργός), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 27:26 (עָשָׂה מְלֶאכֶת הַשָּׂדֶה), I Esther 4:6, 1Ma.14:8 * ;] 
to till the ground: pass., Hébreux 6:7.

G1091.def:
γεώργιον, -ου, τό 
(γεωργός), [in LXX, frequently in Pr., for שָׂדֶה, etc. ;] 
__1. a field (Proverbes 24:5, 30, Strabo). 
__2. cultivation, husbandry, tillage (Proverbes 6:7 9:12, Jérémie 28:23, Sir.27:6): 1 Corinthiens 3:9.
†

G1092.def:
γεωργός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(γῆ, ἔργω = ἔρδω, to do), [in LXX for אִכָּר, etc. ;] 
__1. a husbandman: 2 Timothée 2:6, Jacques 5:7. 
__2. a vine-dresser (cf. ἀμπελουργός, Luc 13:7): Matthieu 21:33-35, 38, 40, 41, Marc 12:1, 2 7, 9, Luc 20:9, 10 14, 16, Jean 15:1.
†

G1094.def:
γῆρας, Attic, genitive (-αος) -ως, dative ᾳ; Ion. and κοινή, -εος (-ους), dative -ει, τό, 
[in LXX for שֵׂיבָה, etc. ;] 
old age: ἐν γήρει, Luc 1:36.†

G1095.def:
γηράσκω (also γηράω; γῆρας), 
[in LXX chiefly for זקן ;] 
to grow old: Jean 21:18, Hébreux 8:13.† 
SYN.: παλαιοῦμαι.

G1096.def:
γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.), 
[in LXX chiefly for היה ;] 
__1. of persons, things occurrences, to come into being, be born, arise, come on: Jean 1:15 8:58, 1 Corinthiens 15:37; a first appearance in public, Marc 1:4, Jean 1:6, al.; before ἐκ (of birth), Romains 1:3, Galates 4:4; διά, Jean 1:3; βροντή, Jean 12:29; σεισμός, Apocalypse 6:12; γογγυσμός, Actes 6:1; χαρά, Actes 8:8, many other similar exx.; ἡμέρα, Luc 22:66, al.; ὀψέ, Marc 11:19; πρωΐα, Matthieu 27:1; νύξ, Actes 27:27. 
__2. Of events, to come to pass, take place, happen: Matthieu 5:18, Marc 5:14, Luc 1:20 2:15, Actes 4:21, 2 Timothée 2:18, al.; μὴ γένοιτο [LXX for חָלִילָה, Jean 22:29, al.], far be it, God forbid: Romains 3:4 (ICC, in l.), 1 Corinthiens 6:15 and frequently in Pl.; καὶ ἐγένετο, ἐγένετο δέ ([in LXX for וַיְהִי ;] see Burton, 142 f.; M, Pr., 16f.; Dalman, Words, 32 f.; Robertson, Gr., 1042 f.), with indic, Matthieu 7:28, Luc 1:8, al.; before καί and indic., Luc 8:1, Actes 5:7, al.; with accusative and inf., Marc 2:23, Luc 3:21, al.; ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο, before τοῦ with inf., Actes 10:25; with dative of person(s), to befall one: with inf., Actes 20:16; with accusative and inf., Actes 22:6; with adv., εὖ, Éphésiens 6:3; τ́ ἐγένετο αὐτῷ (Field, Notes, 115), Actes 7:40 (LXX); before εἰς, Actes 28:6. 
__3. to be made, done, performed, observed, enacted, ordained, etc.: Matthieu 6:10 19:8, Marc 2:27 11:23, Actes 19:26, al.; before διά with genitive, Marc 6:2, Actes 2:43; ὑπό, Luc 13:17; ἐκ, Luc 4:23; ἐν, 1 Corinthiens 9:15; ἀπογραφή, Luc 2:2; ἀνάκρισις Actes 25:26; ἄφεσις, Hébreux 9:22; ὁ νόμος, Galates 3:17; τὸ πάσχα, Matthieu 26:2. 
__4. to become, be made, come to be: with pred., Matthieu 4:3, Luc 4:3, Jean 2:9, 1 Corinthiens 13:11, al.; before ὡς, ὡσεί, Matthieu 10:25, Marc 9:26; εἰς (M, Pr., 71f.), Marc 12:1o, al.; with genitive Apocalypse 11:15; id., of age, Luc 2:42; with dative, γ. ἀνδρί ([LXX for הָיָה לְאִישׁ, Ruth 1:12, al. ;] see Field, Notes, 156), Romains 7:3, 4; before ἐν, Actes 22:17, Apocalypse 1:10, al.; ἐπάνω, Luc 19:19; μετά, with genitive, Mrk.16:[10], Actes 9:19; before εἰς, ἐπί (Field, Notes, 135), κατά (ib., 62), with accusative of place, Actes 20:16 21:35 27:7, al.; before ἐκ, Marc 9:7, Luc 3:22, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:7, al. Aoristic pf. γέγονα (M, Pr., 52, 145f.; Field, Notes, 1f.), Matthieu 25:6, Luc 10:36, al. Aor. ἐγενήθη (for ἐγένετο, M, Pr., 139f.; Mayser, 379), Matthieu 11:23, al. (Cf. απο-, δια-, επι-, παρα-, συμ-, παρα-, προ-.)

G1097.def:
γινώσκω (= γιγν-: see previous word. So also vulgar Attic, in Inscr., see Thumb, MGV, 207), 
[in LXX chiefly for ידע ;] 
to be taking in knowledge, come to know, recognize, perceive, understand; in past tenses to know, realize; pass., to become known: with accusative, Matthieu 22:18, Marc 5:43, Colossiens 4:8, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:5, al. Pass., Matthieu 10:26, Philippiens 4:5, al.; before ὅτι, Matthieu 21:45, Jean 4:1, al.; τί, Matthieu 6:3; ἀπό, Marc 15:45; ὅ, Romains 7:15; τ. λεγόμενα, Luc 18:34; τ. θέλημα, Luc 12:47; τ. καρδίας, Luc 16:15; with accusative of person(s), of recognition by God, 1 Corinthiens 8:3, Galates 4:9; by Christ, neg., Matthieu 7:23; frequently of the knowledge of divine things, of God and Christ; τ. θεόν, Romains 1:21 Galates 4:9; τ. πατέρα, Jean 8:55; τ. κύριον, Hébreux 8:1 (LXX); νοῦν κυρίου, Romains 11:34; Χριστόν, Jean 17:3, 1 Jean 3:6; τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος, 1 Corinthiens 2:14; τ. πνεύμα, 1 Jean 4:6; τ. ἀλήθειαν, Jean 8:32; of Christ's knowledge of the Father (ἐπιγ.), Matthieu 11:27 (Dalman, Words, 282ff.). In Hellenistic writers [LXX for Heb. ידע, Galates 4:1, al.], of sexual intercourse, to know carnally: Matthieu 1:25, Luc 1:34 (Cremer, 153).
SYN.: γ., to know by observation and experience is thus prop. disting. from οἶδα, to know by reflection (a mental process, based on intuition or information); cf. also ἐφίστημι, συνίημι. (Cf. ἀνα-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, προ-γινώσκω.)

G1098.def:
γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό, 
[in LXX for יַיִן, Job 32:19 * ;] 
must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Actes 2:13.†

G1099.def:
γλυκύς, -εῖα, -ύ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מָתוֹק ;] 
Jacques 3:11, 12; opposite to πικρόν, ἁλυκόν, Apocalypse 10:9, 10.†
